claims.text: The dynamic mechanical behavior of as-solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn is governed by a temperature- and strain-rate-dependent transition from dislocation slip to deformation twinning.
The slip-to-twinning transition is manifested by changes in effective activation volumes and activation energies.
The proposed transition underlies the strength-ductility balance of FeNiCrMn.
The as-solidified FeNiCrMn material has a near-equiaxed grain structure and a uniform microstructure.
Strain-rate-jump and stress-relaxation experiments can be used to extract effective activation volumes and energies.
In-situ high-energy X-ray diffraction or high-speed TEM can capture deformation-microstructure evolution during dynamic tensile or compression testing.
The controlled study will span 77 K to 600 K and strain rates covering at least four orders of magnitude.
Activation-volume changes together with the appearance or absence of deformation twins mediate the relationship between microscopic dislocation behavior and macroscopic strength-ductility response.
At higher temperatures and moderate strain rates, FeNiCrMn deforms primarily by thermally activated dislocation slip.
Slip-dominated deformation at higher temperatures and moderate strain rates has a larger effective activation volume.
At lower temperatures or higher strain rates, reduced thermal activation and increased dislocation velocity promote deformation twinning in FeNiCrMn.
The onset of deformation twinning is reflected by a reduction in effective activation volume.
The slip-to-twinning transition governs the dynamic response by balancing strength and ductility.
At room temperature and moderate strain rates, FeNiCrMn should exhibit relatively high activation volume and slip-dominated deformation.
At low temperatures or high strain rates, decreasing activation volume should coincide with the appearance and increasing density of deformation twins.
Room temperature at moderate strain rate provides the slip-dominated baseline.
The hypothesis is restricted to as-solidified, near-equiaxed Co-free FeNiCrMn and may not apply after substantial grain refinement or annealing.
Quantitatively separating solute-drag and phonon-drag contributions is challenging.
The precise temperature and strain-rate thresholds for the proposed transition are uncertain and may vary.
Invariant activation volumes and energies together with no observed microstructural transition across the tested conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
